One shared condition: your buyers commit only when they can see real clients and real numbers. Stories do not close them.

No retail, no e-commerce, no startups, nobody competing on price. Narrowness is what lets us know your buyer better than you do.

Commercial property and related advisory — agents · asset owners · project management · developers · specialist consultants

Established professional and specialist firms whose buyers research before they commit

05 / Why trust a new firm

### Why trust a marketing agency with no track record?

You can't check our references yet, so check everything else. SEMORA STUDIO began operating in 2026 and we say so. Most agencies ask you to trust them and keep the terms for the proposal. Ours are on the site — every price, the published quantities, the one agreed number reviewed at 90 days, and the handover clause. Check them before you write to us.

Beside each of ours is standard practice across the 65 Melbourne firms we reviewed in August 2026.

Industry habit: “Pricing on request.”

08 / SEMORA STUDIO vs a traditional marketing agency

### We are a marketing agency. A narrow one.

Plenty of agencies are excellent, and many are strategic and integrated. This is not a claim that the category is broken.

The difference is shape. Narrower in who we serve. Broader in what we connect. Every price and every delivery time is already published on this site.

Area · Traditional agency engagement · SEMORA STUDIO ·

Market focus · Often many unrelated industries · Commercial industry professionals, owner-led businesses, healthcare practices ·

Starting point · A campaign, website, brand or channel brief · Diagnosis, positioning and a measured baseline ·

Primary output · Creative assets, traffic, reach or leads · A connected client-acquisition and conversion system ·

Positioning · Often delivered as a branding exercise · Connected to fee logic, objections and buyer decisions ·

Sales conversion · May stop once a lead is generated · Enquiry routing, proposals, CRM and follow-up included ·

Pricing · Frequently proposal-based · Products, prices, scope and delivery times published ·

Ownership · Varies by agency · Source files and systems transfer at completion, by contract ·

Who does the work · Varies significantly by size and specialisation · One accountable person on every engagement — Jennifer Wong, who signs off every deliverable before it ships. Research and production are AI-assisted, and we say so ·

Measurement · Campaign or channel metrics · Tied to one agreed commercial number, reviewed at 90 days ·

Track record · An established firm may hold years of references and measured cases · New. Began 2026. One named engagement, AXIS. No verified reviews and no measured client result yet — the first publishes 8 November 2026 ·

Which should you choose? If you have people who can execute but no direction, a consultant may be enough. If your strategy is settled and you only lack production capacity, a specialist agency will do. We are built for the case in between — no senior marketer in-house, and not enough capacity to run it either. See the four products →

### Two ways in.

Already know what you need? A website, the marketing run monthly, a CRM that holds the follow-up. Price it yourself. All 38 services carry a fee and a delivery time, and nothing is sent to you until you send it to us. Not sure where the gap is? Start with the Proof Audit: two weeks, $3,000 + GST, optional, credited in full within 90 days.

A worked example — hypothetical

### How does a SEMORA STUDIO engagement actually run?

In order: the Proof Audit in weeks 0–2 sets the baseline, SIGNAL / in weeks 3–6 sets the position and the one agreed number, / HAUS builds the surfaces in weeks 7–16, and MOMENTUM runs the marketing monthly from month 5. The walk-through below is illustrative, written for a three-partner buyer's advocacy — not a client case. Real cases will publish to the proof standard: named, numbered, dated, caveated.

Weeks 0–2 The Proof Audit

### The baseline, on the record

The practice scores 21/44. Weakest surfaces: named results (0), fee explanation (1), first screen (1). Baseline: one win in four qualified enquiries, the founder in every first call. Fee: $3,000, credited.

Weeks 3–6 SIGNAL /

### The position, and the number

Position: the advocate for time-poor professional purchasers. Fixed fee, with the reasoning written for the website. The contract number: win rate on qualified enquiries.

Weeks 7–16 / HAUS

### The surfaces, built

Six-page site with the fee page and position on screen one. Proposal system. Enquiry response standard — answered by the advocate, same day. Every source file handed over at completion.

Month 5 → MOMENTUM / Shared

### The engine, running

Two editorial pieces and six campaign assets a month. Two proposals built. Monthly reporting against the win rate. The whole thing costs the founder one hour a week.

The recommended start

Start with the audit and it is credited in full within 90 days, which means that if we end up working together the diagnostic costs nothing. Skip it. We set your baseline inside SIGNAL / instead. Either way, no work starts without a number.

# The Proof Audit — SEMORA STUDIO Melbourne
URL: https://www.semora.com.au/proof-audit
Summary: The paid diagnostic and the recommended first step. Two weeks, $3,000 + GST, optional, credited in full.

Product 01 / The diagnostic

## The Proof Audit.

You pay for this one, and we recommend starting here. Two sessions of your time: 90 minutes working, then 60 more for the findings, and a written report you own. It is optional. Skip it, and we set your baseline inside SIGNAL /.

$3,0002 weeks · optional · credited in full · + GST

Scope / what you receive

### What do you get for $3,000?

The instrument · All eleven buyer-facing surfaces scored 0–4, with evidence — the same instrument you can run free ·

Your baseline · Win rate · average fee · founder-hours per win ·

Proposal review · Your last five, against the ones that won ·

The field · Three competitors you name, scored on the same instrument ·

The sequence · The three surfaces to fix, in order, and why ·

The findings · 60-minute session, recorded · written report, yours ·

The instrument

### The eleven surfaces, and the question each one answers.

Somebody who has a problem they have not told anyone about yet checks these, roughly in this order, before they ever speak to you, and by the time the phone rings most of the checking is already done. You do not see any of it. Each is scored 0–4 with the evidence recorded beside it. Score yourself first, free →

# · Surface · What the buyer is asking ·

01 · First screen · Do these people operate at my level? ·

02 · The enquiry response · How fast, by whom — and did they read what I wrote? ·

03 · The proposal · Is this a document worth keeping? ·

04 · Named results · Has this worked for someone like me, with a number attached? ·

05 · Third-party evidence · Does anyone outside the firm vouch for them? ·

06 · The practitioner's track record · Has this person personally done the thing? ·

07 · Peer proof · Who else in my world already uses them? ·

08 · The fee explanation · Is the price reasoned, or is it a number? ·

09 · What happens after · Do they stay, or hand over and go? ·

10 · The physical impression · The office, the print, the room we meet in. ·

11 · Consistency across all ten · Do I get the same firm every time I look? ·

The order of work

### How long does the Proof Audit take, and what do you have to do?

Two weeks, and ninety minutes of your time. You give us two things: one 90-minute working session, and your last five proposals. Nothing else is asked of you. Nothing waits on your team.

Then, in order. We score the eleven surfaces against evidence, and we set your baseline: win rate on qualified enquiries, average fee, founder-hours per win. Then your proposals. Your last five, read against the ones that won. Then the three competitors you name, scored on the same instrument, and if that list is the wrong one, if the firm actually taking your work is not on it, we say so and we say why. Last comes the part you actually wanted: the three surfaces to fix, ranked, with the reason each one sits where it does.

It ends with a 60-minute findings session, recorded, and a written report. The recording and the report are yours.

Why it is paid

### Why does SEMORA STUDIO charge for an audit when others give one away?

Because a free audit is a sales call in a costume, and specialists can tell. Charging makes it an engagement rather than a pitch, and an engagement is the version whose findings you can actually use, because nothing is held back for a proposal at the end. That is the trade. It also filters for people who are actually going to act on them.

You keep the report whether or not you hire us.

The $3,000 is credited in full against any engagement you start within 90 days. Hire us and the audit costs nothing. Walk away and you still hold a scored baseline, and a ranked list of what to fix in what order, which is more than you had on the Monday morning you first picked up the phone to us. That is the deal.

What it is not

### What is the Proof Audit not?

Not a strategy, and not a proposal. It measures where you stand. It does not decide your position, write your messaging or build anything, and if you want the audit to hand you a strategy at the end you will be disappointed. That is deliberate. That work is SIGNAL / and / HAUS, priced separately and published in the same detail.

It is also optional. You can start at SIGNAL / instead and we set the baseline there in week one. The rule underneath all of it is no work without a baseline, because otherwise nobody can say at 90 days whether anything moved. That rule does not bend.

Book the Proof Audit Next: SIGNAL / →

# SIGNAL / the position — SEMORA STUDIO Melbourne
URL: https://www.semora.com.au/signal
Summary: What you stand for, to whom, and why it is worth your fee. Four weeks, from $14,000 + GST — core scope plus optional modules.

Product 02 / The position

## SIGNAL /

What you stand for, who it is for, and why it is worth your fee. Two half-days and two reviews of your time. Best entered from the audit. Otherwise we set the baseline in week one.

from $14,0004 weeks · core scope + optional modules · + GST

Scope / what you receive

### What do you get with SIGNAL /?

Deliverable · What it is · What it does commercially ·

The position · Statement + the argument that defends it · The written answer to “why you, at your fee” ·

The proposition & fee logic · What you sell, and the reasoning that holds the price · Read by buyers before they ever ask — ends the discount conversation ·

Message architecture · Promise → idea → position → elevator → service story · Every person in the practice says the same thing ·

The audience optional · +$1,800 · Definition + two personas from your actual client base · Who to say it to, and what they check before buying ·

The objection playbook · Your six objections, answered in your words · Scripted for first calls and proposals — no improvising under pressure ·

The competitive map optional · +$1,900 · Where you sit against named competitors — and where not to go · Stops you marketing into ground you cannot win ·

The number · One agreed metric, set from your baseline · What all following work is accountable to, in the contract ·

The handover · The written document + a 90-minute team session · Repeatable by a new hire without you in the room ·

Core scope is $14,000 fixed. The two optional modules take the ceiling to $17,700 — chosen at kickoff, not mid-engagement.

Why it is priced like this

### Why does SIGNAL / cost $14,000?

Because a position is fee infrastructure, and the $14,000 is measured against what an undefended position costs you in a year. Open last year's client list. Beside each name, write the fee you first quoted and the fee you actually took to win the work. Add up the gap. That is what one undefended year costs you, and the same gap opens again this year, and the year after that, because nothing about the conversation that produced those discounts has changed since the last time you had it. Nobody enjoys that sum. For most practices it is a multiple of this fee. Run it in your own books before you talk to us.

Six objections come up on a first call, and you answer them a different way each time, because nobody ever wrote down the best version. That is the leak. The position, the fee logic and the objection playbook exist to end that discount. Check the arithmetic against your own books. That is the only claim we make for it.

What this is not

### Not a workshop with sticky notes.

Hand the document to whoever starts on Monday. On day one they can repeat it correctly, without you in the room. Written down, or it is not a position.

Start with the audit Next: / HAUS →

Quantities are published on purpose. A retainer that says “content as needed” can mean four pieces or none, and by month three nobody in the room can remember what was agreed, so we write the number down and you hold us to it. The comparison

### How does MOMENTUM compare with hiring a marketing manager?

MOMENTUM is priced against a hire, not against an agency. Shared comes to $88,800 a year, under a Marketing Specialist on $80k–$95k plus super. Held comes to $162,000, under a Head of Marketing on $172,500 plus super. Both salary figures are from SEEK's published Melbourne marketing salary data, 2026. What a salary also buys is somebody in the building, which a retainer does not, so the fair comparison is the list above against one person's week.

# About SEMORA STUDIO — Melbourne marketing agency
URL: https://www.semora.com.au/about
Summary: SEMORA STUDIO is a Melbourne specialist growth company and marketing agency for commercial industry, owner-led and healthcare practices. Published prices.

About

## What is SEMORA STUDIO?

SEMORA STUDIO is a leading specialist growth company and marketing agency for commercial industry professionals, owner-led businesses, and healthcare and allied-health practices. We combine positioning, digital marketing, AI visibility and conversion systems into clearly defined products with transparent pricing and measurable performance.

01 / Who we work with

### Who does SEMORA STUDIO work with?

Three fields, one condition. Commercial industry professionals — commercial property and the advice around it: agents, asset and property owners, project management, developers and specialist consultants.

Owner-led businesses. Firms with a name on the door and a founder still in the room. The kind whose buyers read everything before they call. Not retail. Not online stores. Not a startup before its first revenue, and not anyone whose pitch is the cheapest price in the market.

Healthcare and allied health practices. Clinics with more than one practitioner. Health advertising is regulated in Australia. So every clinical claim we write is checked against the National Law and against current Ahpra guidance, we write down what backs it, and it does not go live until you have read it and said yes. That is slower. We keep that record so you can produce it. It is not legal advice, and we will tell you when to get some.

The shared condition: your buyers must need to see real clients and real outcomes before they commit. That rules out plenty of good businesses, and we would rather say so on the first call than three months into a retainer you are already paying for. So here it is. If a good story on its own wins your market, we are the wrong firm.

Who we are not for: retail, e-commerce, startups pre-revenue, and anyone competing on price. Narrowness is what lets us know your buyer better than you do.

# Our clients — SEMORA STUDIO Melbourne
URL: https://www.semora.com.au/clients
Summary: Who we act for, and the standard every published result must meet: named, dated, verified. One named engagement, AXIS. No verified reviews yet, and we say so.

Reviews, results and evidence

## What we can actually prove.

It comes down to two questions. Who else have you done this for, and can I ring them? SEMORA STUDIO began operating in 2026, so the honest answer is short. We will not manufacture a longer one. Everything we can prove is on this page, sorted into four kinds of evidence, so you can see which is which.

Kind of evidence · What it means · Status today ·

Verified client reviews · Direct client words, published with written permission and a name · None yet ·

Measured client results · Baseline, what we changed, the outcome, the period, and the caveats · First one at the 90-day review ·

Named engagements · Work we are contracted to deliver, named with permission · 1 — AXIS ·

Illustrative examples · Hypothetical, written by us to show a format. Not testimonials · Labelled as samples ·

01 / Verified client reviews

### Are there verified SEMORA STUDIO client reviews?

None yet, and we will say so. A verified review, to SEMORA STUDIO, means one thing. A real client, in their own words, with a name, a role, a date and written permission to print it. We have none. Not one. And we will not dress up something weaker to fill the gap, so you will not find praise here from a client we decline to name, or a tidy line we wrote that a client nodded at, or five stars signed with a single initial. We ask at the 90-day review.

Client words land on this page, or they land nowhere.

Regulated health services are the harder case. The National Law prohibits clinical testimonials in advertising, so we will not publish one at all, and that binds us exactly as it binds the clinic.

02 / Measured client results

### How does SEMORA STUDIO publish a client result?

To a six-part template, published early and listed below: the baseline, the intervention, the result, the period, the caveats and the client's written permission. A result publishes only when it has all six. Miss one and Jennifer Wong holds it back. That rule is the reason this section is still empty today, and we would rather you saw an empty section than a number with no baseline underneath it. It is the same proof standard the rest of the method runs on.

### The baseline

What was true before we started, measured, with the date

### The intervention

What we actually did — scope, not adjectives

### The result

The agreed number, measured the same way as the baseline

### The period

Start and end dates, so you can judge the sample

### The caveats

What else changed, what we did not control, what the number excludes

### The permission

Named and approved by the client, or it does not appear

Proof,not promises.

One, named: AXIS, which advises on commercial property. That is work we are signed to deliver, named because the client agreed to be named. Being signed is not the same as being measured. The measured result publishes at the 90-day review on 8 November 2026.

# Method — SEMORA STUDIO Melbourne
URL: https://www.semora.com.au/method
Summary: One agreed number reviewed at 90 days, everything handed over, and our own eleven-surface score published — zeros included.

Method

## Accountable to one number. In writing.

A named metric in the contract, everything handed over at completion — and our own instrument applied to us, in public.

### How does SEMORA STUDIO work?

01

### What is the one number SEMORA STUDIO is accountable to?

One metric from your audit baseline — win rate, fee integrity, or founder dependency — reviewed at 90 days, on the record. The full accountability clause is in legal drafting and publishes here when signed off: a commitment before it is enforceable would be a claim we could not evidence.

02

### What do you own at the end of an engagement?

Everything SEMORA STUDIO built for you. Source files, tokens, templates and the written governance model transfer at completion, by contract. SIL OFL fonts — no seat licences. Nothing held hostage to a retainer.

03

### Why hire a marketing agency that has no track record yet?

SEMORA STUDIO is new, and says so, unprompted. What substitutes for tenure: named people, this published method, published prices, and source files that transfer by contract — if we vanished tomorrow, you keep everything.

04 / Our own score

24 of a possible 44, at launch in August 2026, zeros included. It is the same eleven-surface instrument we score clients on and the same one published free at score your practice — eleven surfaces, each scored 0–4, so 44 is the ceiling. The zeros are the honest cost of being new, and the plan for removing them is beside each one. Re-scored quarterly.
